You can work from up to 12 references, separate the result into up to five audio stems, and move from a 768p draft to 4K finishing.

More room to experiment, refine, and keep the details that make a generation feel like a film.

What does Pika H3 Flex do with a tiny, silly film idea?

The test: a small lavender octopus versus a claw machine it has no business beating, in an arcade soaked with rain. Neon bouncing off puddles, a nosy seagull, panicked joystick fixes, a lucky double grab and a wildly excessive victory dance. One simple prompt became a pocket-sized cinematic comedy.

virals.name: Artificial Analysis
virals.text:
We are launching AA-Video-I2V v2.1 and AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1, our new benchmark for evaluating image to video models. It judges every model at up to 1080p on a new set of image and text prompts, and ranks models across 10 use cases, 10 capabilities and a diverse range of visual styles.

Image to video makes AI video production more controllable. Creators start from a product shot, a storyboard frame or a character design that needs to move. A strong model keeps the people, objects and setting of the starting image consistent while delivering the motion, camera work and sound the prompt asks for.

In our benchmark, every prompt pairs a 1080p starting image with a prompt written for that image, and is tagged by use case (such as Marketing & Advertising and Live-Action Film), by the capability it tests (such as Human Anatomy and Text Rendering), and by visual style. The overall ranking samples evenly across use cases and capabilities, so it reflects a model's versatility, not just its best category.

We are launching AA-Video-I2V v2.1 with more than 58,000 human preference votes from private evaluators based in the US/UK over 1,000 prompts, and AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1 with more than 44,000 votes over 500 prompts. Only 5% of our prompts are available on the public arena, keeping the evaluation resistant to public set contamination, with the prompts rotated every month.

Initial insights from the top of the AA-Video-I2V v2.1 Leaderboard:

➤ Dreamina Seedance 2.5 ranks #1 overall, statistically tied with Seedance 2.0 and the MiniMax H3 family, and leads 11 category boards, more than any other model, including Human Anatomy, Camera Control and Retail & Ecommerce. At $34.12/min it is the most expensive model in the top 10.

➤ Dreamina Seedance 2.0 ranks #2 and is #1 on Audio Synchronization and Lighting & Materials.

➤ MiniMax H3 (768p), an open weights model, ranks #3 at $4.80/min, about 1/7 of the price of Seedance 2.5. It is #1 on Text Rendering.

➤ MiniMax H3 Max, post-trained by fal, ranks #4 with audio and #1 on AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1, and leads Spatio-Temporal Consistency and UI/UX & Motion Design.

➤ Bach 1.0 Pro from Video Rebirth ranks #3 on AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1, statistically tied for #1, at $7.20/min.

See below for how image to video differs from text to video, and the use case, capability and style breakdowns 🧵

virals.name: Beginnersblog
virals.text:
Your AI video looks cinematic… until the next shot.

That's where most AI-generated films fall apart.

The problem isn't always video quality. It's continuity.

A character looks left in one shot, then suddenly looks right. A coffee cup changes hands. A door moves to another wall.

Each shot looks perfect. But together, something feels wrong.

Here's what traditional filmmakers understand:

→ 180-degree rule: Keep cameras on one side of the action line to preserve screen positions.

→ Eyeline match: Characters should look toward each other's established positions.

→ Match on action: If someone starts opening a door, the next shot should continue that movement.

→ Prop continuity: Objects shouldn't change positions without a reason.

→ Lighting and scale: Shadows and physical proportions must remain believable.

Before generating your next shot, check three things:
- Where is everything positioned?
- What action is happening at the cut?
- What must remain unchanged?

The secret to believable AI filmmaking isn't generating better individual shots. It's making every shot connect.
.
.

→ One 5 s video costs 10 of your 16 free credits
→ Text to video hit a paywall after one video

Text to image 8/10

Free tier value 4/10

Text to video: not tested (paywall)

Use it for quick AI images or a short clip from your own picture.

→ Fix the image upload

outsiders.text:
We are launching AA-Video-I2V v2.1 and AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1, our new benchmark for evaluating image to video models. It judges every model at up to 1080p on a new set of image and text prompts, and ranks models across 10 use cases, 10 capabilities and a diverse range of visual styles.

Image to video makes AI video production more controllable. Creators start from a product shot, a storyboard frame or a character design that needs to move. A strong model keeps the people, objects and setting of the starting image consistent while delivering the motion, camera work and sound the prompt asks for.

In our benchmark, every prompt pairs a 1080p starting image with a prompt written for that image, and is tagged by use case (such as Marketing & Advertising and Live-Action Film), by the capability it tests (such as Human Anatomy and Text Rendering), and by visual style. The overall ranking samples evenly across use cases and capabilities, so it reflects a model's versatility, not just its best category.

We are launching AA-Video-I2V v2.1 with more than 58,000 human preference votes from private evaluators based in the US/UK over 1,000 prompts, and AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1 with more than 44,000 votes over 500 prompts. Only 5% of our prompts are available on the public arena, keeping the evaluation resistant to public set contamination, with the prompts rotated every month.

Initial insights from the top of the AA-Video-I2V v2.1 Leaderboard:

➤ Dreamina Seedance 2.5 ranks #1 overall, statistically tied with Seedance 2.0 and the MiniMax H3 family, and leads 11 category boards, more than any other model, including Human Anatomy, Camera Control and Retail & Ecommerce. At $34.12/min it is the most expensive model in the top 10.

➤ Dreamina Seedance 2.0 ranks #2 and is #1 on Audio Synchronization and Lighting & Materials.

➤ MiniMax H3 (768p), an open weights model, ranks #3 at $4.80/min, about 1/7 of the price of Seedance 2.5. It is #1 on Text Rendering.

➤ MiniMax H3 Max, post-trained by fal, ranks #4 with audio and #1 on AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1, and leads Spatio-Temporal Consistency and UI/UX & Motion Design.

➤ Bach 1.0 Pro from Video Rebirth ranks #3 on AA-Video-I2V-Silent v2.1, statistically tied for #1, at $7.20/min.

See below for how image to video differs from text to video, and the use case, capability and style breakdowns 🧵

outsiders.name: Beginnersblog
outsiders.text:
Your AI video looks cinematic… until the next shot.

That's where most AI-generated films fall apart.

The problem isn't always video quality. It's continuity.

A character looks left in one shot, then suddenly looks right. A coffee cup changes hands. A door moves to another wall.

Each shot looks perfect. But together, something feels wrong.

Here's what traditional filmmakers understand:

→ 180-degree rule: Keep cameras on one side of the action line to preserve screen positions.

→ Eyeline match: Characters should look toward each other's established positions.

→ Match on action: If someone starts opening a door, the next shot should continue that movement.

→ Prop continuity: Objects shouldn't change positions without a reason.

→ Lighting and scale: Shadows and physical proportions must remain believable.

Before generating your next shot, check three things:
- Where is everything positioned?
- What action is happening at the cut?
- What must remain unchanged?

The secret to believable AI filmmaking isn't generating better individual shots. It's making every shot connect.
.
.

outsiders.text:
I spent $0 and 14 of 16 free credits testing @ClipflyOfficial.

The image was clean and one video worked. Then the free credits ran out before my hard test, and the eraser added an object that was not there.

Access: free account with Google sign-in. 15 sign-up credits plus 1 daily check-in credit from the Rewards Center. No card, no social tasks.

What I tested
Easy: text to image, laptop showing "HONEST AI REVIEWS". Under 30 s, 2 credits
Typical: animate my own title card with a push in and steam. About 1 min, 10 credits
Hard: text to video, reviewer turns laptop to show 7/10. Blocked, needed 10 credits, had 4
Extra: editor text overlay export (free) and Magic Eraser on a mug (2 credits, about 15 s)

What it does well
→ Image text spelled right on the first try, 1920x1080
→ Image to video kept my layout and text and added the motion I asked for
→ Every download I made was free with no watermark, editor exports 1080p free

What it does badly
→ One 5 s video costs 10 of your 16 free credits
→ Text to video hit a paywall after one video
→ Magic Eraser removed the mug and painted a fake plant in its place
→ Upload failed twice before it worked
→ Video came out 864x480 from a 720p input
→ Slow: blank home page and a Loading screen of about a minute each
→ Google sign-in says "Fotor", not Clipfly

Pricing as listed
Pro $10.99/mo (200 credits)
Pro+ $39.99/mo (1,000 credits)
Business $87.99/mo (3,000 credits)
Yearly from $49.99. Free credits expire in 90 days

Scores
Text to image 8/10
Image to video 7/10
Video editor 6/10
Magic Eraser 4/10
Free tier value 4/10
Speed and UI 5/10
Text to video: not tested (paywall)

Verdict 5.7/10
Use it for quick AI images or a short clip from your own picture.
Skip it if you want to test text to video for free.

What I would fix first
→ Enough free credits for two video tries
→ Fix the image upload
→ Eraser should fill background, not add objects
→ Faster first load, fewer popups

Tip: make your image first (2 credits), then spend your 10 video credits animating it. Bookmark this before you sign up.

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
